title: From Label Priors to Task Evidence: Long-Video Frame Selection via Bayesian GRPO
claim: Supervised label priors give a good initialization, and refining the selector with a frozen model's answer likelihood as dense reward aligns selection with task needs.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, dashed zoom-in from (a) to (b)
description: A three-panel framework figure with rounded boxes on a cream, pink and light-blue palette. Panel (a), Keyframe Selector, is a vertical stack of fire-marked Video-Text Fusion Transformer blocks (×N) below a Scoring Head. Question-text and video-frame feature tokens enter at the bottom, and importance scores such as 0.2, 0.5 and 0.0 come out at the top. Panel (b), Label Prior, shows the selector with frozen text and vision towers, a question and a film strip. Two histograms compare label logits with predicted logits, joined by 'update' arrows. Panel (c), Task Evidence, shows Group Sampling feeding sampled frame subsets and the question into a frozen multimodal LLM. The LLM outputs an answer, NLL rewards R1–R4, advantages A1–A4 and the reward and advantage formulas. Snowflake icons mark frozen modules and flame icons mark trained ones.
caption: The overall framework of our methods. (a) Keyframe Selector. The lightweight selector ($f_\theta$) comprises stacked Video-Text Fusion Transformers. It modulates frame features with query semantics to output importance logits, then parameterizing a Plackett-Luce distribution. (b) Stage I: Label Prior Elicitation. We utilize keyframe label annotations to construct a Label Prior. The selector is trained via pairwise ranking loss to align its predicted logits with the label logits, establishing a robust initialization. (c) Stage II:Task-Evidence Posterior Inference. We freeze the MLLM and treat it as a frozen task environment. The selector performs Group Sampling to propose discrete frame subsets ($z$). The MLLM evaluates these subsets to provide dense NLL rewards ($R$) and advantages ($A$). The policy is refined via Bayesian GRPO to maximize task evidence while maintaining KL-regularization towards the label prior.
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) face significant scalability challenges in long-video understanding due to quadratic attention complexity and context window constraints. Existing retrieval-based approaches typically rely on supervised learning from static keyframe annotations. However, these label priors often fail to align with the actual information required by downstream MLLMs for complex reasoning, creating a misalignment between the training target and inference needs. To bridge this gap, we propose a probabilistic framework that reformulates frame selection as latent-variable inference. We first initialize a lightweight policy using supervised learning to capture general visual saliency. Then, we treat a frozen MLLM as a task environment and use its answer likelihood as dense task evidence to refine the policy via Bayesian Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Within this formulation, the negative log-likelihood (NLL) over ground-truth answer tokens provides a principled dense reward, while a prior-matching KL term preserves semantic consistency with the elicited label prior. This process transitions the selection principle from static label priors to task evidence. Extensive experiments on Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench demonstrate that our selector achieves competitive accuracy with MLLM-based scorers while retaining the inference efficiency of lightweight methods. The selector is trained once with a frozen MLLM environment and transfers directly to multiple downstream MLLMs without retraining. Code is available at github.com/Miraclecsc/Frame_Selection_GRPO
